title: Fundamental Duties can't be enforced by a court, yet courts use them
sources: Constitution of India, Part IVA, Article 51A (inserted by the Constitution (Forty-second Amendment) Act, 1976; clause (k) added by the Constitution (Eighty-sixth Amendment) Act, 2002)
AIIMS Students' Union v. AIIMS, Supreme Court: duties equally important as rights; aid to interpretation (as reported by Anantam IAS and Vajiram and Ravi)
M.C. Mehta v. Union of India (1988) and later environmental cases citing Article 51A(g) (secondary sources)

quiz.q: Which amendment added Article 51A to the Constitution?
quiz.why: Right. The 42nd Amendment (1976) inserted Part IVA and Article 51A with ten duties; the 86th (2002) only added clause (k).

script: No court can force you to perform a Fundamental Duty.
So why do judges keep citing them?

right.label: Interpret

claims.claim: The 42nd Amendment (1976) inserted Part IVA and Article 51A with ten Fundamental Duties
The 86th Amendment (2002) added Article 51A(k): parents/guardians to provide opportunities for education to children between 6 and 14 years
Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable: courts cannot directly enforce them
In AIIMS Students' Union v. AIIMS the Supreme Court said duties are equally important as rights and relevant to interpreting laws
Courts have relied on Article 51A(g) (duty to protect and improve the natural environment) in environmental cases, e.g. M.C. Mehta (1988), M.K. Ranjitsinh (2024)

review_note: Spec written after the fact for the existing video and Sarvam recording; spoken text matches 18-fundamental-duties.voice.txt word for word. Still no primary source: the Constitution text of Article 51A and the AIIMS judgment were not fetched. The AIIMS year differs across sources (Vajiram 2001, Anantam 2002), so no year is shown.
